chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who is standing in the obligatory prayer and forgets his bag or belongings, fearing their loss or destruction. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He cuts his prayer and secures his belongings, then he resumes the prayer.' I said: 'If he is in the obligatory prayer and an animal escapes from him, or his animal escapes, so he fears it will go away or he will suffer hardship from it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with him cutting his prayer.'
ai.seo_question: Can a person break their obligatory prayer to save their belongings from being lost or stolen?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of Samaanah, clarifies the juristic principle of 'darar' (harm/loss) in prayer, distinguishing between minor distractions and significant property loss. It establishes that preserving wealth from ruin takes precedence over maintaining the continuity of the obligatory prayer, allowing the worshipper to break, secure the item, and resume. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing spiritual devotion with practical necessity, ensuring that religious obligations do not lead to undue financial hardship.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked himasws about the man who happens to be standing in the Obligatory Salāt, so he remembers his bad or his provisions, fearing its wastage or its destruction. Heasws said: ‘He can cut off his Salāt and protect his belongings. Then he should re-commence the Salāt’. I said, ‘Supposing he happens to be in the Obligatory (Salāt), and an animal flees, or his animal flees, so he fears that it would go away or he would suffer hardship due to it’. So heasws said: ‘There is no problem with if he were to cut off his Salāt’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah who has said the following: “

I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is standing in obligatory Salah (prayer) when he remembers his bag or property and he is afraid of loss or destruction of such items. He (the Imam) said, ‘He can discontinue his Salah (prayer) to secure such items then perform his Salah (prayer) again.’ I then asked him (the Imam), ‘What happens if he is in obligatory Salah (prayer) when a stumper (animal) or his stumper escapes and he is afraid of its getting lost or causing him difficulties?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful if he discontinues his Salah (prayer).”’
